changes.why: 'The click meter started' only means something if you see the taxi-meter drawing, and the TTS read מונה as 'muna'. Eyes-closed the plain fact is: every click costs money, nobody calls.
'Every click takes a coin' is the jar drawing; a click costs shekels, not a coin, so by ear it sounds like nonsense.
'The meter is ticking' depends on the taxi-meter picture; with the screen off there is no meter, just money leaving on clicks.
Same meter line as the hook; replaced with the plain money fact so it lands without the drawing.
'Three coins' is the drawing; the plain fact is he paid for three clicks and the phone never rang.
Not an eyes-closed failure; brand moved to the approved plain-text form (מוואו) so the automatic TTS swap handles pronunciation. Price wording unchanged.
Same meter line as the hook; replaced with the plain money fact.
